english: A sector of a circle has a constant area of $25\ \text{cm}^{2}$, while its radius $r$ and its central angle vary with time. At the instant when $r=4$ cm, the central angle is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{45}{\pi}$ degrees per second. Then the rate of change of the perimeter of the sector (in cm per second) at that instant is ______.
hindi: किसी वृत्त के एक त्रिज्यखण्ड का क्षेत्रफल अचर $25\ \text{cm}^{2}$ है, जबकि इसकी त्रिज्या $r$ तथा केन्द्रीय कोण समय के साथ परिवर्तित होते हैं। जिस क्षण $r=4$ cm है, उस क्षण केन्द्रीय कोण $\dfrac{45}{\pi}$ अंश प्रति सेकण्ड की दर से घट रहा है। तब उस क्षण त्रिज्यखण्ड के परिमाप के परिवर्तन की दर (cm प्रति सेकण्ड में) ______ है।
solution_full: Work with the central angle $\theta$ in radians, since the formulas $s=r\theta$ (arc) and $\dfrac12r^{2}\theta$ (area) hold only in radians. $1^{\circ}=\dfrac{\pi}{180}$ rad, so the given rate is $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=-\dfrac{45}{\pi}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{180}=-\dfrac14$ rad per second.
Constant area: $\dfrac12r^{2}\theta=25\Rightarrow \theta=\dfrac{50}{r^{2}}$. At $r=4$: $\theta=\dfrac{50}{16}=\dfrac{25}{8}$ radian, which is less than $2\pi$, so the sector exists.

Differentiating $\theta=50r^{-2}$: $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=-\dfrac{100}{r^{3}}\dfrac{dr}{dt}$. At $r=4$: $-\dfrac14=-\dfrac{100}{64}\dfrac{dr}{dt}\Rightarrow \dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{64}{400}=0.16$ cm/s (the radius grows as the angle shrinks).
So the perimeter is decreasing at $0.18$ cm/s at that instant.
originality_note: New: a sector kept at constant area while its angle shrinks at a rate given in degrees (way 5); the perimeter rate needs the radian conversion, the constraint and two chained rates. Closest known: maximum area of a sector of given perimeter. Different because: the area is fixed instead of the perimeter, the data rate is in degrees, and the asked rate is of the perimeter.

concept_use.Rate measure and related rates: d theta/dt = -100 r^-3 dr/dt and dP/dt = (2 - 50/r^2) dr/dt chain the rates.

key_step: Convert the angular rate to radians, use the constant-area constraint to get dr/dt, then differentiate the perimeter.
